title: Publicly verifiable quantum money from quantum-secure LWE alone
formal: Does polynomial-hard Learning With Errors against quantum polynomial-time adversaries suffice for publicly verifiable quantum money, without obfuscation or any other computational assumption?
definitions: A bank generates a public verification key and a secret minting key. A banknote consists of a serial number and a quantum state. Anyone can verify it using the public key, while a polynomial-time quantum counterfeiter given valid notes should not produce more accepted notes than it received. The intended construction is in the standard model, with no ideal random oracle and no extra trusted setup.

context_blocks.text: Quantum money seeks a publicly checkable object that cannot be copied even by its legitimate holder. Deriving that property from a familiar lattice assumption would substantially clarify its cryptographic foundations.

The cited construction of anonymous public-key quantum money uses additional assumptions, including obfuscation. Anonymous notes and voting are consequences of a stronger construction; their existence under those assumptions does not establish ordinary public quantum money from LWE alone.

why: Base quantum unclonability with public verification on a standard computational assumption.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
